weaknesses.title: MKTEMPDIR always under system TMP not CUBALC_STATE
weaknesses.detail: Same isolation gap as MKTEMP. Agent workspaces scatter in /tmp; multi-tenant hosts share namespace. No DIR=STATE option.

weaknesses.title: RMDIR non-empty only soft-fails; no recursive cleanup
weaknesses.detail: Agents must RM each child then RMDIR. No RMDIR -r / RMALL-dir. Orphan /tmp trees accumulate on partial cleanup.

weaknesses.title: BASE64 is text/string plane — not binary-safe file stream
weaknesses.detail: No BASE64FILE path encode. Binary artifacts need READ (may truncate/null) then BASE64. Agents cannot stamp opaque blobs cleanly.

weaknesses.title: WRITEATOMIC b64 plate omits trailing NL
weaknesses.detail: c3RhdHVzPXJlYWR5 without $; readers that require line-oriented plates glue.

weaknesses.title: Empty CUBALC_ARG1 blocked for encode/decode empty string
weaknesses.detail: Language BASE64 "" works; agent ARG empty → needs text EXIT. Cannot test empty round-trip via ARG path.

weaknesses.title: MKTEMP vs MKTEMPDIR dual family; no auto-cleanup
weaknesses.detail: File temps vs dir temps; no scoped session GC for either.

weaknesses.title: RMDIR missing soft N=0 OK=1 looks like success
weaknesses.detail: Idempotent miss same shape as success except N; agents must check RMDIR_N.

workarounds: Copy workspace under STATE if isolation required
RM all children then RMDIR; or RMALL bag of files
Prefer text payloads for BASE64; HASHFILE for binary identity
Digit-check REQUIRE; check RMDIR_N after cleanup
Track open dirs in plate for GC on exit
language_gaps: ARG empty-string vs missing for encode ""
issues_faced: TMP isolation and no recursive rmdir are sharp gaps
